findings.evidence: Linux v6.12 THP monitoring documentation limits AnonHugePages coverage to PMD-sized anonymous THP; smaller mTHP uses PTE mappings. task_mmu.c accounts smaps anonymous_thp in smaps_pmd_entry.
findings.consequence: The previous unqualified instruction to measure AnonHugePages could allow zero to be treated as absence of all THP even while discussing per-size controls.
findings.fix: Make the blind spot explicit in the main rule and existing THP reference; distinguish meminfo host scope from smaps process PMD mappings. No universal disablement policy added.

findings.evidence: Linux v6.12 huge_memory.c sum_mthp_stat aggregates per-CPU statistics by size, with anon_fault_alloc exposed through DEFINE_MTHP_STAT_ATTR; the THP guide defines it as a successful fault-allocation event.
findings.consequence: Using per-size counters to fill AnonHugePages coverage without preserving scope could wrongly attribute host allocation activity or resident bytes to the affected JVM.
findings.fix: Read relevant available per-size fields conditionally, use same-host/size interval deltas, retain reset/unavailable status, and leave JVM attribution unresolved. Policy and latency changes require additional supporting evidence.

+Separate policy, residency and allocation activity. On Linux 6.12, `AnonHugePages` in
+`/proc/meminfo` reports system PMD-sized anonymous THP; the fields in `/proc/<pid>/smaps`
+cover that process's PMD mappings. They do not count smaller PTE-mapped mTHP. A zero value
+therefore does not establish that all anonymous THP is absent. Read `smaps` only as needed;
+frequent scans add overhead.
+
+When smaller sizes matter, inspect the deployed kernel's available
+`/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/hugepages-<size>kB/stats` fields. For example,
+`anon_fault_alloc` counts successful fault allocations: compare same-host, same-size deltas
+over the incident window, retaining reset/unavailable status. Those host-wide events are
+neither a process attribution nor a count of pages still resident. A rising 64 KiB counter
+beside zero JVM `AnonHugePages` can coexist without proving either use or non-use by that
+JVM. Leave that attribution unresolved until targeted evidence supports it; neither signal
+alone justifies changing THP policy or blaming it for a latency spike.
